expected_effect: No action proposed, so no effect is expected. Nothing about the system should change as a result of this proposal. Concretely: none of the three buildable actions has its preconditions met. rollback_image requires a prior image tag and a deploy/image change inside the window — frontend's change log holds only a service-object creation and a first container creation at 17:31:55, with no predecessor image recorded [tr_57fd4b831076], and the same is true for the only other service with change data, consul [tr_c4d033b6d797]. revert_config requires a prior configuration and a config change inside the window — again only a creation record exists, and the one configured address under suspicion (consul:8500) was demonstrated to become reachable without any change [tr_b46c4a6267a3]. restart_service requires evidence pointing at process state: the only process-state signal is a cold start at 17:31:56 whose discovery-refusal burst ended at 17:32:00 and never recurred, leaving ~6.5 clean minutes before the 17:38:25 onset [tr_b46c4a6267a3] — restarting frontend would re-run exactly the bootstrap race that was already ruled out as the onset mechanism. The correct next step is investigative, not remedial: an untruncated frontend log query covering 17:32:00–17:38:30, and per-service logs for the five unmeasured downstream edges.
if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if a subsequent untruncated log slice over 17:32:00–17:38:30 shows a mechanism that one of rollback_image, revert_config or restart_service addresses — for example renewed consul:8500 refusals continuing through onset (would point at consul process state), a frontend OOM/goroutine-leak or connection-pool-exhaustion signature (would point at restart_service on frontend), or a downstream service logging errors from a recorded image or config change inside the window (would point at rollback or revert on that service). It is also wrong if a stakeholder judges that a blind frontend restart is cheap enough to try despite an unknown mechanism; I do not, because the only measured consequence of a frontend cold start in this incident is a 4-second total discovery outage across all five backends [tr_b46c4a6267a3]. Note separately that no action taken here could be confirmed by metrics: frontend and user have no span-derived series in either the incident or baseline window [tr_9e57cb00ad61][tr_3c200821e5c6] and frontend emitted zero traces for the hour [tr_e4ec257e6a74], so the only available confirmation channel is Loki logs. An unobservable fix is a second reason to hold.
risk: The risk of abstaining is that the incident continues unmitigated while the alert is live, and the time spent on further investigation is time the alerted frontend stays degraded. If the true mechanism is a frontend process-state fault that a restart would clear, this abstention leaves it running. Against that: acting on a low-confidence 'unknown' verdict risks a restart that recreates the known 17:31:56 bootstrap race, producing a fresh all-backend discovery gap and destroying the in-process state and the very log continuity needed to find the real cause — converting an unexplained degradation into a second, self-inflicted one with the original still undiagnosed.
blast_radius: No service is touched, so no caller sees a change. For contrast, the action not taken: a frontend restart would be seen by every external client of frontend and would momentarily break its outbound edges to user, recommendation, profile, search and reservation during re-resolution; a restart or rollback of any one of those five would be seen by frontend as reset connections on that edge. The investigative follow-ups proposed instead (log and metric queries) are read-only and visible to nobody.
